title: Sednit_Dropper_Investigation_df3
description: Investigate a compromised system to identify and analyze the Sednit dropper and its associated artifacts.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Sednit group is known for using sophisticated malware toolkits designed for espionage and long-term monitoring of targeted systems. One of their tools, Seduploader, is a dropper used to deliver other malicious payloads such as Xagent and Xtunnel. Your task is to investigate a compromised system to identify and analyze the Sednit dropper and its associated artifacts.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the compromised host. Check the systemd service files in the /etc/systemd/system directory for any unusual or recently created services.
levels.solution: Check the systemd service files in the /etc/systemd/system directory for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services are managed through service files located in the /etc/systemd/system directory. These files define how services should be started, stopped, and managed.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the 'ls' command to list the service files in the /etc/systemd/system directory.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for services that were recently created or modified, as these could indicate malicious activity.

levels.title: Determine Scheduled Task
levels.content: Determine whether a scheduled task or timer is responsible for automatically executing suspicious activity. Look for timer files in the /etc/systemd/system directory that correspond to the suspicious service identified in the previous task.
levels.solution: Look for timer files in the /etc/systemd/system directory that correspond to the suspicious service identified in the previous task.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd timers are used to schedule tasks at specific intervals. Timer files are typically located in the /etc/systemd/system directory and have a .timer extension.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the 'ls' command to list the timer files in the /etc/systemd/system directory.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for timers that correspond to the suspicious service identified in the previous task, as these could indicate automated malicious activity.

levels.title: Locate Malicious Files
levels.content: Locate files introduced onto the system by the malicious software. Investigate unusual or hidden directories, especially those created around the time of the suspected compromise.
levels.solution: Investigate unusual or hidden directories, especially those created around the time of the suspected compromise.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malicious software often creates files in unusual or hidden directories to avoid detection. These directories can be found using the 'ls' command with appropriate options.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the 'ls -la' command to list all files and directories, including hidden ones, in the /tmp directory.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for directories or files that were created around the time of the suspected compromise, as these could indicate the presence of malicious software.
